3009: inline_always_inline_functions (struct cgraph_node *node)
3010: {
3011:   struct cgraph_edge *e;
3012:   bool inlined = false;
3013:
3014:   for (e = node->callees; e; e = e->next_callee)
3015:     {
3016:       struct cgraph_node *callee = e->callee->ultimate_alias_target ();
3017:       gcc_checking_assert (!callee->aux || callee->aux == (void *)(size_t)1);
3018:       if (!DECL_DISREGARD_INLINE_LIMITS (callee->decl)
3019:           /* Watch for self-recursive cycles.  */
3020:           || callee->aux)
3021:         continue;
3022:
3023:       if (e->recursive_p ())
3024:         {
3025:           if (dump_enabled_p ())
3026:             dump_printf_loc (MSG_MISSED_OPTIMIZATION, e->call_stmt,
3027:                              "  Not inlining recursive call to %C.\n",
3028:                              e->callee);
3029:           e->inline_failed = CIF_RECURSIVE_INLINING;
3030:           continue;
3031:         }
3032:       if (callee->definition
3033:           && !ipa_fn_summaries->get (callee))
3034:         compute_fn_summary (callee, true);
3035:
3036:       if (!can_early_inline_edge_p (e))
3037:         {
3038:           /* Set inlined to true if the callee is marked "always_inline" but
3039:              is not inlinable.  This will allow flagging an error later in
3040:              expand_call_inline in tree-inline.cc.  */
3041:           if (lookup_attribute ("always_inline",
3042:                                  DECL_ATTRIBUTES (callee->decl)) != NULL)
3043:             inlined = true;
3044:           continue;
3045:         }
3046:
3047:       if (dump_enabled_p ())
3048:         dump_printf_loc (MSG_OPTIMIZED_LOCATIONS, e->call_stmt,
3049:                          "  Inlining %C into %C (always_inline).\n",
3050:                          e->callee, e->caller);
3051:       inline_call (e, true, NULL, NULL, false);
3052:       callee->aux = (void *)(size_t)1;
3053:       /* Inline recursively to handle the case where always_inline function was
3054:          not optimized yet since it is a part of a cycle in callgraph.  */
3055:       inline_always_inline_functions (e->callee);
3056:       callee->aux = NULL;
3057:       inlined = true;
3058:     }
3059:   return inlined;

215: init_dont_simulate_again (void)
216: {
217:   basic_block bb;
218:   bool saw_a_complex_op = false;
219:
220:   FOR_EACH_BB_FN (bb, cfun)
221:     {
222:       for (gphi_iterator gsi = gsi_start_phis (bb); !gsi_end_p (gsi);
223:            gsi_next (&gsi))
224:         {
225:           gphi *phi = gsi.phi ();
226:           prop_set_simulate_again (phi,
227:                                    is_complex_reg (gimple_phi_result (phi)));
228:         }
229:
230:       for (gimple_stmt_iterator gsi = gsi_start_bb (bb); !gsi_end_p (gsi);
231:            gsi_next (&gsi))
232:         {
233:           gimple *stmt;
234:           tree op0, op1;
235:           bool sim_again_p;
236:
237:           stmt = gsi_stmt (gsi);
238:           op0 = op1 = NULL_TREE;
239:
240:           /* Most control-altering statements must be initially
241:              simulated, else we won't cover the entire cfg.  */
242:           sim_again_p = stmt_ends_bb_p (stmt);
243:
244:           switch (gimple_code (stmt))
245:             {
246:             case GIMPLE_CALL:
247:               if (gimple_call_lhs (stmt))
248:                 {
249:                   sim_again_p = is_complex_reg (gimple_call_lhs (stmt));
250:                   switch (gimple_call_combined_fn (stmt))
251:                     {
252:                     CASE_CFN_CABS:
253:                       /* Expand cabs only if unsafe math and optimizing. */
254:                       if (optimize && flag_unsafe_math_optimizations)
255:                         saw_a_complex_op = true;
256:                       break;
257:                     default:;
258:                     }
259:                 }
260:               break;
261:
262:             case GIMPLE_ASSIGN:
263:               sim_again_p = is_complex_reg (gimple_assign_lhs (stmt));
264:               if (gimple_assign_rhs_code (stmt) == REALPART_EXPR
265:                   || gimple_assign_rhs_code (stmt) == IMAGPART_EXPR)
266:                 op0 = TREE_OPERAND (gimple_assign_rhs1 (stmt), 0);
267:               else
268:                 op0 = gimple_assign_rhs1 (stmt);
269:               if (gimple_num_ops (stmt) > 2)
270:                 op1 = gimple_assign_rhs2 (stmt);
271:               break;
272:
273:             case GIMPLE_COND:
274:               op0 = gimple_cond_lhs (stmt);
275:               op1 = gimple_cond_rhs (stmt);
276:               break;
277:
278:             default:
279:               break;
280:             }
281:
282:           if (op0 || op1)
283:             switch (gimple_expr_code (stmt))
284:               {
285:               case EQ_EXPR:
286:               case NE_EXPR:
287:               case PLUS_EXPR:
288:               case MINUS_EXPR:
289:               case MULT_EXPR:
290:               case TRUNC_DIV_EXPR:
291:               case CEIL_DIV_EXPR:
292:               case FLOOR_DIV_EXPR:
293:               case ROUND_DIV_EXPR:
294:               case RDIV_EXPR:
295:                 if (TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (op0)) == COMPLEX_TYPE
296:                     || TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (op1)) == COMPLEX_TYPE)
297:                   saw_a_complex_op = true;
298:                 break;
299:
300:               case NEGATE_EXPR:
301:               case CONJ_EXPR:
302:               case PAREN_EXPR:
303:                 if (TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (op0)) == COMPLEX_TYPE)
304:                   saw_a_complex_op = true;
305:                 break;
306:
307:               case REALPART_EXPR:
308:               case IMAGPART_EXPR:
309:                 /* The total store transformation performed during
310:                   gimplification creates such uninitialized loads
311:                   and we need to lower the statement to be able
312:                   to fix things up.  */
313:                 if (TREE_CODE (op0) == SSA_NAME
314:                     && ssa_undefined_value_p (op0))
315:                   saw_a_complex_op = true;
316:                 break;
317:
318:               default:
319:                 /* When expand_complex_move would trigger make sure we
320:                    perform lowering even when there is no actual complex
321:                    operation.  This helps consistency and vectorization.  */
322:                 if (TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (gimple_op (stmt, 0))) == COMPLEX_TYPE)
323:                   saw_a_complex_op = true;
324:                 break;
325:               }

329:     }

6947:   bitint_big_endian = false;
6948:
6949:   unsigned int i;
6950:   for (i = 0; i < num_ssa_names; ++i)
6951:     {
6952:       tree s = ssa_name (i);
6953:       if (s == NULL)
6954:         continue;
6955:       tree type = TREE_TYPE (s);
6956:       if (TREE_CODE (type) == COMPLEX_TYPE)
6957:         {
6958:           if (arith_overflow_arg_kind (SSA_NAME_DEF_STMT (s))
6959:               != bitint_prec_small)
6960:             break;
6961:           type = TREE_TYPE (type);
6962:         }
6963:       if (TREE_CODE (type) == BITINT_TYPE
6964:           && bitint_precision_kind (type) != bitint_prec_small)
6965:         break;
6966:       /* We need to also rewrite stores of large/huge _BitInt INTEGER_CSTs
6967:          into memory.  Such functions could have no large/huge SSA_NAMEs.  */
6968:       if (SSA_NAME_IS_VIRTUAL_OPERAND (s))
6969:         {
6970:           gimple *g = SSA_NAME_DEF_STMT (s);
6971:           if (is_gimple_assign (g) && gimple_store_p (g))
6972:             {
6973:               tree t = gimple_assign_rhs1 (g);
6974:               if (TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (t)) == BITINT_TYPE
6975:                   && (bitint_precision_kind (TREE_TYPE (t))
6976:                       >= bitint_prec_large))
6977:                 break;
6978:             }
6979:         }
6980:       /* Similarly, e.g. with -frounding-math casts from _BitInt INTEGER_CSTs
6981:          to floating point types need to be rewritten.  */
6982:       else if (SCALAR_FLOAT_TYPE_P (type))
6983:         {
6984:           gimple *g = SSA_NAME_DEF_STMT (s);
6985:           if (is_gimple_assign (g) && gimple_assign_rhs_code (g) == FLOAT_EXPR)
6986:             {
6987:               tree t = gimple_assign_rhs1 (g);
6988:               if (TREE_CODE (t) == INTEGER_CST
6989:                   && TREE_CODE (TREE_TYPE (t)) == BITINT_TYPE
6990:                   && (bitint_precision_kind (TREE_TYPE (t))
6991:                       != bitint_prec_small))
6992:                 break;
6993:             }
6994:         }
6995:     }
6996:   if (i == num_ssa_names)
6997:     return 0;

1357:     {
1358:       for (gsi = gsi_start_bb (bb); !gsi_end_p (gsi); gsi_next (&gsi))
1359:         {
1360:           /* Give the target first try at replacing the instruction.  */
1361:           cfg_changed |= targetm.instruction_selection (fun, &gsi);
1362:

1364:              calls mapping to supported optabs.  */
1365:           gimple *g = gimple_expand_vec_cond_expr (&gsi);
1366:           if (g != NULL)
1367:             {
1368:               tree lhs = gimple_assign_lhs (gsi_stmt (gsi));
1369:               gimple_set_lhs (g, lhs);
1370:               gsi_replace (&gsi, g, false);
1371:             }
1372:
1373:           /* Recognize .VEC_SET and .VEC_EXTRACT patterns.  */
1374:           cfg_changed |= gimple_expand_vec_set_extract_expr (fun, &gsi);
1375:           if (gsi_end_p (gsi))

7990: ix86_minimum_incoming_stack_boundary (bool sibcall)
7991: {
7992:   unsigned int incoming_stack_boundary;
7993:
7994:   /* Stack of interrupt handler is aligned to 128 bits in 64bit mode.  */
7995:   if (cfun->machine->func_type != TYPE_NORMAL)
7996:     incoming_stack_boundary = TARGET_64BIT ? 128 : MIN_STACK_BOUNDARY;
7997:   /* Prefer the one specified at command line. */
7998:   else if (ix86_user_incoming_stack_boundary)
7999:     incoming_stack_boundary = ix86_user_incoming_stack_boundary;
8000:   /* In 32bit, use MIN_STACK_BOUNDARY for incoming stack boundary
8001:      if -mstackrealign is used, it isn't used for sibcall check and
8002:      estimated stack alignment is 128bit.  */
8003:   else if (!sibcall
8004:            && ix86_force_align_arg_pointer
8005:            && crtl->stack_alignment_estimated == 128)
8006:     incoming_stack_boundary = MIN_STACK_BOUNDARY;
8007:   else
8008:     incoming_stack_boundary = ix86_default_incoming_stack_boundary;
8009:
8010:   /* Incoming stack alignment can be changed on individual functions
8011:      via force_align_arg_pointer attribute.  We use the smallest
8012:      incoming stack boundary.  */
8013:   if (incoming_stack_boundary > MIN_STACK_BOUNDARY
8014:       && lookup_attribute ("force_align_arg_pointer",
8015:                            TYPE_ATTRIBUTES (TREE_TYPE (current_function_decl))))
8016:     incoming_stack_boundary = MIN_STACK_BOUNDARY;
8017:
8018:   /* The incoming stack frame has to be aligned at least at
8019:      parm_stack_boundary.  */
8020:   if (incoming_stack_boundary < crtl->parm_stack_boundary)
8021:     incoming_stack_boundary = crtl->parm_stack_boundary;
8022:
8023:   /* Stack at entrance of main is aligned by runtime.  We use the
8024:      smallest incoming stack boundary. */
8025:   if (incoming_stack_boundary > MAIN_STACK_BOUNDARY
8026:       && DECL_NAME (current_function_decl)
8027:       && MAIN_NAME_P (DECL_NAME (current_function_decl))
8028:       && DECL_FILE_SCOPE_P (current_function_decl))
8029:     incoming_stack_boundary = MAIN_STACK_BOUNDARY;
8030:
8031:   return incoming_stack_boundary;
8032: }
8033:
8034: /* Update incoming stack boundary and estimated stack alignment.  */
8035:
8036: static void
8037: ix86_update_stack_boundary (void)
8038: {
8039:   ix86_incoming_stack_boundary
8040:     = ix86_minimum_incoming_stack_boundary (false);
8041:
8042:   /* x86_64 vararg needs 16byte stack alignment for register save area.  */
8043:   if (TARGET_64BIT
8044:       && cfun->stdarg
8045:       && crtl->stack_alignment_estimated < 128)
8046:     crtl->stack_alignment_estimated = 128;
8047:
8048:   /* __tls_get_addr needs to be called with 16-byte aligned stack.  */
8049:   if (ix86_tls_descriptor_calls_expanded_in_cfun
8050:       && crtl->preferred_stack_boundary < 128)
8051:     crtl->preferred_stack_boundary = 128;
8052:
8053:   /* For 32-bit MS ABI, both the incoming and preferred stack boundaries
8054:      are 32 bits, but if force_align_arg_pointer is specified, it should
8055:      prefer 128 bits for a backward-compatibility reason, which is also
8056:      what the doc suggests.  */
8057:   if (lookup_attribute ("force_align_arg_pointer",
8058:                         TYPE_ATTRIBUTES (TREE_TYPE (current_function_decl)))
8059:       && crtl->preferred_stack_boundary < 128)
8060:     crtl->preferred_stack_boundary = 128;
8061: }
8062:
8063: /* Handle the TARGET_GET_DRAP_RTX hook.  Return NULL if no DRAP is
8064:    needed or an rtx for DRAP otherwise.  */
8065:
8066: static rtx
8067: ix86_get_drap_rtx (void)
8068: {
8069:   /* We must use DRAP if there are outgoing arguments on stack or
8070:      the stack pointer register is clobbered by asm statement and
8071:      ACCUMULATE_OUTGOING_ARGS is false.  */
8072:   if (ix86_force_drap
8073:       || ((cfun->machine->outgoing_args_on_stack
8074:            || crtl->sp_is_clobbered_by_asm)
8075:           && !ACCUMULATE_OUTGOING_ARGS))
8076:     crtl->need_drap = true;
8077:
8078:   if (stack_realign_drap)
8079:     {
8080:       /* Assign DRAP to vDRAP and returns vDRAP */
8081:       unsigned int regno = find_drap_reg ();

8091:       seq = end_sequence ();

8094:       if (!optimize)

8098:         }

8100:     }
8101:   else
8102:     return NULL;
8103: }

13013: ix86_tls_address_pattern_p (rtx op)
13014: {
13015:   subrtx_var_iterator::array_type array;
13016:   FOR_EACH_SUBRTX_VAR (iter, array, op, ALL)
13017:     {
13018:       rtx op = *iter;
13019:       if (MEM_P (op))
13020:         {
13021:           rtx *x = &XEXP (op, 0);
13022:           while (GET_CODE (*x) == PLUS)
13023:             {
13024:               int i;
13025:               for (i = 0; i < 2; i++)
13026:                 {
13027:                   rtx u = XEXP (*x, i);
13028:                   if (GET_CODE (u) == ZERO_EXTEND)
13029:                     u = XEXP (u, 0);
13030:                   if (GET_CODE (u) == UNSPEC
13031:                       && XINT (u, 1) == UNSPEC_TP)
13032:                     return true;
13033:                 }
13034:               x = &XEXP (*x, 0);
13035:             }
13036:
13037:           iter.skip_subrtxes ();
13038:         }
13039:     }
13040:
13041:   return false;
13042: }
```

803: /* Return true if the single edge between blocks A and B is the only place
804:    in RTL which holds some unique locus.  */
805:
806: static bool
807: unique_locus_on_edge_between_p (basic_block a, basic_block b)
808: {
809:   const location_t goto_locus = EDGE_SUCC (a, 0)->goto_locus;
810:   rtx_insn *insn, *end;
811:
812:   if (LOCATION_LOCUS (goto_locus) == UNKNOWN_LOCATION)
813:     return false;
814:
815:   /* First scan block A backward.  */
816:   insn = BB_END (a);
817:   end = PREV_INSN (BB_HEAD (a));
818:   while (insn != end && (!NONDEBUG_INSN_P (insn) || !INSN_HAS_LOCATION (insn)))
819:     insn = PREV_INSN (insn);
820:
821:   if (insn != end && loc_equal (INSN_LOCATION (insn), goto_locus))
822:     return false;
823:
824:   /* Then scan block B forward.  */
825:   insn = BB_HEAD (b);
826:   if (insn)
827:     {
828:       end = NEXT_INSN (BB_END (b));
829:       while (insn != end && !NONDEBUG_INSN_P (insn))
830:         insn = NEXT_INSN (insn);
831:
832:       if (insn != end && INSN_HAS_LOCATION (insn)
833:           && loc_equal (INSN_LOCATION (insn), goto_locus))
834:         return false;
835:     }
836:
837:   return true;
838: }
839:
840: /* If the single edge between blocks A and B is the only place in RTL which
841:    holds some unique locus, emit a nop with that locus between the blocks.  */
842:
843: static void
844: emit_nop_for_unique_locus_between (basic_block a, basic_block b)
845: {
846:   if (!unique_locus_on_edge_between_p (a, b))
847:     return;
848:
849:   BB_END (a) = emit_insn_after_noloc (gen_nop (), BB_END (a), a);
850:   INSN_LOCATION (BB_END (a)) = EDGE_SUCC (a, 0)->goto_locus;
851: }

73: control_flow_insn_p (const rtx_insn *insn)
74: {
75:   switch (GET_CODE (insn))
76:     {
77:     case NOTE:
78:     case CODE_LABEL:
79:     case DEBUG_INSN:
80:       return false;
81:
82:     case JUMP_INSN:
83:       return true;
84:
85:     case CALL_INSN:
86:       /* Noreturn and sibling call instructions terminate the basic blocks
87:          (but only if they happen unconditionally).  */
88:       if ((SIBLING_CALL_P (insn)
89:            || find_reg_note (insn, REG_NORETURN, 0))
90:           && GET_CODE (PATTERN (insn)) != COND_EXEC)
91:         return true;
92:
93:       /* Call insn may return to the nonlocal goto handler.  */
94:       if (can_nonlocal_goto (insn))
95:         return true;
96:       break;
97:
98:     case INSN:
99:       /* Treat trap instructions like noreturn calls (same provision).  */
100:       if (GET_CODE (PATTERN (insn)) == TRAP_IF
101:           && XEXP (PATTERN (insn), 0) == const1_rtx)
102:         return true;
103:       if (!cfun->can_throw_non_call_exceptions)
104:         return false;
105:       break;
106:
107:     case JUMP_TABLE_DATA:
108:     case BARRIER:
109:       /* It is nonsense to reach this when looking for the
110:          end of basic block, but before dead code is eliminated
111:          this may happen.  */
112:       return false;
113:
114:     default:
115:       gcc_unreachable ();
116:     }
117:
118:   return can_throw_internal (insn);

3492: split_insn (rtx_insn *insn)
3493: {
3494:   /* Split insns here to get max fine-grain parallelism.  */
3495:   rtx_insn *first = PREV_INSN (insn);

3497:   rtx insn_set, last_set, note;
3498:
3499:   if (last == insn)
3500:     return NULL;
3501:
3502:   /* If the original instruction was a single set that was known to be
3503:      equivalent to a constant, see if we can say the same about the last
3504:      instruction in the split sequence.  The two instructions must set
3505:      the same destination.  */
3506:   insn_set = single_set (insn);
3507:   if (insn_set)
3508:     {
3509:       last_set = single_set (last);
3510:       if (last_set && rtx_equal_p (SET_DEST (last_set), SET_DEST (insn_set)))
3511:         {
3512:           note = find_reg_equal_equiv_note (insn);
3513:           if (note && CONSTANT_P (XEXP (note, 0)))
3514:             set_unique_reg_note (last, REG_EQUAL, XEXP (note, 0));
3515:           else if (CONSTANT_P (SET_SRC (insn_set)))
3516:             set_unique_reg_note (last, REG_EQUAL,
3517:                                  copy_rtx (SET_SRC (insn_set)));
3518:         }
3519:     }
3520:
3521:   /* try_split returns the NOTE that INSN became.  */

3523:

3525:      splitters instead of computing the proper hard register.  */

480:       seq = end_sequence ();
481:       target_spill_cost [speed] = seq_cost (seq, speed);

1: with Ada.Text_IO;
2: with Silver_IO;
3:
4: package Silver_Arguments with SPARK_Mode => On is
5:    --  Both queries observe the immutable GNAT argument vector. An absent
6:    --  argument selects Default; one valid argument preserves its exact bytes,
7:    --  including the empty String. Invalid input is handled by the caller's
8:    --  required validity guard and Reject branch, never printed as a fallback.
9:    function Input_Is_Valid return Boolean with Global => null;
10:
11:    --  Return canonical one-based bounds while preserving the selected bytes.
12:    --  This also applies to shifted and null-range Default values.
13:    function First_Or_Default (Default : String) return String
14:      with Global => null,
15:           Post => First_Or_Default'Result'First = 1
16:             and then First_Or_Default'Result'Length <= Silver_IO.Max_Length
17:             and then (Input_Is_Valid or else First_Or_Default'Result'Length = 0)
18:             and then (for all Ch of First_Or_Default'Result =>
19:               Character'Pos (Ch) in 32 .. 126);
20:
21:    procedure Reject
22:      with Global => (In_Out => Ada.Text_IO.File_System), Always_Terminates;
23: end Silver_Arguments;
```

## src/silver_io.ads (selected Silver API, complete)

```text
1: with Ada.Text_IO;
2: package Silver_IO with SPARK_Mode => On is
3:    --  Application membership restricts literals separately. The executable
4:    --  guard makes this implementation safe for every String argument.
5:    Max_Length : constant Positive := 4_096;
6:    --  Static observations record bytes only after successful libc calls.
7:    --  GNAT erases this verification state and its assertions from execution.
8:    Written_Bytes : String (1 .. Max_Length + 1) := (others => Character'Val (0))
9:      with Ghost => Static;
10:    Written_Count : Natural range 0 .. Max_Length + 1 := 0 with Ghost => Static;
11:    Flushed : Boolean := False with Ghost => Static;
12:    Succeeded : Boolean := False with Ghost => Static;
13:    --  Succeeded records acceptance of every input byte and LF followed by a
14:    --  successful fflush(NULL). On detected failure, set process exit status 1
15:    --  and return normally with Succeeded False. The admitted Main then returns
16:    --  with that status. Success leaves the startup success status unchanged.
17:    --  Environmental blocking is modeled by Always_Terminates => False.
18:    procedure Put_Line (Item : String)
19:      with Global => (In_Out => Ada.Text_IO.File_System,
20:                      Output => (Written_Bytes, Written_Count, Flushed, Succeeded)),
21:           Always_Terminates => False,
22:           Post => (Static => Succeeded = Flushed
23:             and then (if Succeeded then Item'Length <= Max_Length
24:               and then Written_Count = Item'Length + 1
25:               and then Written_Bytes (1 .. Item'Length) = Item
26:               and then Written_Bytes (Written_Count) = Character'Val (10)));
27:    --  Put has the same completion/failure behavior without appending LF.
28:    --  Even an empty Item requests a flush; later success never clears failure.
29:    procedure Put (Item : String)
30:      with Global => (In_Out => Ada.Text_IO.File_System,
31:                      Output => (Written_Bytes, Written_Count, Flushed, Succeeded)),
32:           Always_Terminates => False,
33:           Post => (Static => Succeeded = Flushed
34:             and then (if Succeeded then Item'Length <= Max_Length
35:               and then Written_Count = Item'Length
36:               and then Written_Bytes (1 .. Item'Length) = Item));
37: end Silver_IO;
```
